text: Ὁ ῥαπίσας, etc. Malchus Chrysostomo, hom. 82 in Joannem ; Theophani Cerameo, hom. 27 ; Euthymio, aliis. Unde apud Lambecium, De bibliotheca Cæsarea, lib. iv, cod. 164, n. 7, quæstio de nomine ejus qui Christum percussit. Et lib. v, cod. 289, p. 243, inter Georgii Calybæ ἐρωταποκρίσεις, tricesima secunda est, περὶ τοῦ ῥαπίσαντος τὸν Χριστόν · Servum illum Caiphæ, qui in Domini cam Christi faciem colaphum impegerat. In Damasceno orat. 2 de assumptione Deiparæ. Cyrilli vero Alexandrini sententiam omnes norunt.
anchorLine: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ῥαπίσας (q) ἐπὶ τῆς σιαγόνος
en: 'The one who struck', etc. Malchus, in Chrysostom, hom. 82 on John; in Theophanes Cerameus, hom. 27; Euthymius; others. Hence in Lambecius, On the Caesarean Library, bk 4, cod. 164, n. 7, the question of the name of him who struck Christ. And bk 5, cod. 289, p. 243, among the Questions and Answers of George Calybes, the thirty-second is 'On the one who struck Christ': that servant of Caiaphas who struck the face of Christ with a blow. In Damascene, oration 2 on the Assumption of the Mother of God. Everyone knows the opinion of Cyril of Alexandria.
plateNote: Left column ends 'qui in Domini', right column begins 'cam Christi faciem' as printed; 'cam' is on the plate.

text: Λεκτικίῳ. t. I, p. 413 B, epis. t. 14 S. Chrysostomi, in Vita Maximi confessoris, n. 39 ; Vita et Martyrio S. Eudociæ, n. 39, et apud alios a Meursio citatos. Hinc λεκτικάριος, etiam in epistola Theodoriti 110 ; Anonymus in Vita Chrysostomi, Savilianæ editionis, t. VIII, p. 358 ; l. ix et xvi, λεκτίκιον habet, forsan non absque menda. Porro locus e Vita Maximi dignus est qui hic ascribatur, Ἐπεὶ δὲ, ὡς ὁ λόγος ἔφη, πρὸς τὴν ὑπερορίαν τὸν θεῖον ἀπήνεγκαν Μάξιμον, πολλὰ μὲν συνέβη τοῦτον παθεῖν κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ πολλὰς ὑπομεῖναι τὰς ἀλγηδόνας, οἷα μήτ᾽ εἰς λεκτίκιον καθεσθῆναι δυνάμενον, τῷ πάντῃ κατειργάσθαι τοῖς πόνοις, καὶ ταῖς μυρίαις τετρυχῶσθαι ὀδύναις. Ἀμέλει καὶ εἴς τι χαλάδριον βέργεσι πεπλεγμένον τοῦτον ἐνθέμενοι μόλις καὶ κόπῳ διαβαστάζοντες, τὴν μακρὰν ὁδὸν ἐκείνην ἀπήγαγον. S. Maximum itaque, ut relatum est, in exsilium deportatum, contigit in via multa pati, multasque subire ærumnas, et doloribus conflictari, cum nec jumento nec lectica sedere posset, omnino scilicet confectus laboribus, innumerisque angoribus attritus. Quamobrem gestatorio vimineo grabbato imponunt, et vix ægreque gestantes, longo illo itinere abducunt. Quia per illum emendatio et lux oboritur vocabulo corrupto et obscuro, quod legitur in Vita Dosithei apud Dorotheum Corderii : Ἐστρώννυε δὲ τοῖς ἀῤῥώστοις πάνυ καλῶς· τοιοῦτος δὲ ἦν περὶ τὸν λογισμὸν ἐλευθέριος καὶ ἐξαγγελτικός, ὅτι πολλάκις ἐν ὅσῳ ἐφιλοκάλει στρῶσαι, εἶδε τὸν μακάριον παρερχόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, κύριε, λέγει μοι ὁ λογισμός, Καλῶς στρωννύεις. Καὶ ἀπεκρίνατο ἐκεῖνος, Βαβαί, κύριε, ἰδοὺ εἶ καλὸς βρεγγάριος vel βρεγκάριος· μὴ γὰρ καλὸς μοναχός. Apparet enim ex βέργεσι scribi debere βεργάριος, Virgarius, hoc est stratorum vimineorum adornator. Cæterum ægrotis lectulos commodissime sternebat : adeo autem ingenuus et liber erat in cogitationibus suis manifestandis, ut non raro cum lectulos egregie stravisset, ac beatum Dorotheum illuc transire videret, ei diceret : Domine, domine, cogitatio mihi dicit, eleganter lectulos sternis ; et respondit ei ille : Papæ domine, ecce bonus es virgarius, lectorum seu ex virgis stratorum constructor, non vero bonus monachus

text: Ἠλίαν. Φλαβιανόν. Non facile concesserim Theodoreto lectori ac Theophani chronographo, Heliam Hierosolymorum et Flavianum Antiochenum anathema dixisse concilio Chalcedonensi. Colligo magis ex Evagrio et Nicephoro, atque ex Cyrillo Scythopolitano in Vita S. Sabæ, loco citato, act. 1 et 5 synodi vii, beatos antistites multa quidem variaque œconomia, necnon erga Anastasium imperatorem adulatione usos fuisse, numquam tamen aperte voluisse synodum anathematizare. Quo de ultimo Soterichus et Xenaias hæretici querelas ad imperatorem detulerunt, referente ipso Theophane.
anchorLine: Ἠλίαν μὲν εἰς Αἰλὰν, Φλαβιανὸν (u) δὲ εἰς Πέτραν.
en: 'Elias. Flavian.' I should not readily grant that Theodore the Lector and Theophanes the chronographer are right that Elias of Jerusalem and Flavian of Antioch anathematized the Council of Chalcedon. I gather rather from Evagrius, Nicephorus and Cyril of Scythopolis (Life of St Sabas, place cited; acts 1 and 5 of the seventh synod) that the blessed prelates used much and varied accommodation and flattery toward the emperor Anastasius, yet never openly wished to anathematize the synod. On this last point the heretics Soterichus and Xenaias brought complaints to the emperor, as Theophanes reports.

text: Μακεδόνιον. Exsilium Macedonii verbis memoralibus et valde observandis refertur a Liberato, Breviarii, cap. 19 : Hoc tempore, inquit, Macedonius Constantinopolitanus episcopus, ab Imperatore Anastasio dicitur expulsus, tamquam Evangelia falsasset, et maxime illud Apostoli dictum : « Quia apparuit in carne, justificatum est in spiritu. » Hunc enim immutasse, ubi habet, ὃς, id est qui, monosyllabum Græcum, littera mutata o in ω vertisse, et fecisse ὡς, id est, ut esset Deus, apparuit per carnem. Tanquam Nestorianus ergo culpatus expellitur per Severum monachum. Et primo quidem ad ea : Quia apparuit in carne, observo, Liberatum, I Tim. iii, 16, aut legisse in Græco ὡς, aut Latinum
anchorLine: Μακεδόνιον (x) τοὺς πατριάρχας Κωνσταντινουπό-
en: 'Macedonius.' The exile of Macedonius is reported in memorable and much-to-be-observed words by Liberatus, Breviary ch. 19: 'At this time,' he says, 'Macedonius, bishop of Constantinople, is said to have been expelled by the emperor Anastasius as though he had falsified the Gospels, and especially that saying of the Apostle: "Who was manifested in the flesh, justified in the spirit."' [It is said] that he changed hos ('who'), a Greek monosyllable, by altering o to omega, making hos ('as'), i.e. 'that he might be God, he appeared through the flesh'. Accused as a Nestorian, he is expelled through the monk Severus. And first, as to 'Who was manifested in the flesh': I observe that Liberatus (1 Tim. 3:16) either read hos in the Greek, or the Latin [breaks off].
plateNote: Note breaks off at the foot of the page at 'Latinum'.
